notes: RETRY 2026-09-04, original attempt (all 3 standard tiers) was BLOCKED - see prior failure_reason/notes preserved in git history / prior JSON version. This retry used curl_cffi TLS-impersonation profile brute-force per the alternate-network-path toolkit. robots.txt re-checked: no Claude-specific (anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web/etc.) disallow; generic disallows cover SiteMapView, Search?, cart, checkout, THDLogon, etc. and specifically /b/Featured-Products* but NOT /b/Holiday-Decorations* or any other /b/ category path used here - so this is a bot-protection wall, not a policy opt-out. BREAKTHROUGH: brute-forced 11 curl_cffi impersonation profiles (chrome116/119/120/124/131, safari17_0/18_0, safari18_0_ios, safari184_ios, edge99/101) against https://www.homedepot.com/b/Holiday-Decorations/N-5yc1vZbd6e - chrome124/120/119/116/safari17_0/safari18_0 all 403'd instantly (matches original Tier-1 finding); chrome131/safari17_0 returned a thin 200 (2507 bytes, actual Akamai block-page in disguise, not usable); safari18_0_ios and safari184_ios (iOS Safari TLS fingerprint) both returned genuine 200 with full page content (872KB), past the same Akamai wall that blocked every other route in the original attempt. Homepage itself always 200 across nearly all profiles (never the bottleneck). WHAT WAS RECOVERED: the successful iOS-Safari-fingerprint fetch of the Holiday Decorations root page, and of one leaf page (Christmas Trees, N-5yc1vZc3rz, fetched before the WAF re-blocked this fingerprint - see below), returned server-rendered Next-style React state (window.__APOLLO_STATE__, valid JSON, ~88KB on the root page) containing THE SITE'S OWN genuine navigation/taxonomy objects (VisualNavigationItem tiles on the root landing page, plus a SideNavigation/Navigation sidebar list on the Christmas Trees leaf page) with real titles, real canonical /b/... category URLs, and (on the Christmas Trees leaf) a confirmed SearchModel breadcrumb trail (Holiday Decorations > Christmas Decorations > Christmas Trees) plus 24 real BaseProduct entries (with prices, images, review counts) proving it is a genuine product-listing page, not an empty or fabricated node. QTY LIMITATION (important): this __APOLLO_STATE__ payload is a 'browse/landing' render (visual tiles + a capped ~24-item top-sellers shelf) and carries NO total-count/pagination field anywhere (SearchMetadata has only canonicalUrl; searchReport has only keyword=null) - the true product-grid view that would show 'Showing X of Y' lives behind the query param ?catStyle=ShowProducts, and that specific URL variant returned 403 on EVERY profile tested (chrome116/119/120/124/131, safari17_0/18_0/18_0_ios/184_ios), and also 403'd via r.jina.ai reader proxy (confirmed: 'Warning: Target URL returned error 403: Forbidden') and 400'd via translate.goog (www-homedepot-com.translate.goog, Google's own edge rejected the request, likely Google's own bot-check, tried _x_tr_tl=es). Per the shared qty rule (never estimate/infer/copy), every row below is recorded qty:null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag rather than guessing from the visible ~24-item shelf. RATE-LIMIT NOTE: after roughly 25-30 rapid requests (across profile brute-force + one-off verification calls, no delay), the working safari18_0_ios/safari184_ios fingerprint itself got blocked (403) even on the exact same root/Christmas-Trees URLs that had just succeeded, and stayed blocked through a session-with-cookies+4s-delay retry and a further ~20-45s cooldown - this is very likely a short-lived Akamai bot-score escalation triggered by request burst rate rather than a URL-specific rule (the homepage kept returning 200 throughout). Because of this, only the ROOT Holiday Decorations page and the Christmas Trees leaf were individually content-verified (real product data present) before the block kicked back in; the remaining leaf URLs below were NOT individually re-fetched for content verification - they are included because their category title AND canonical URL were read directly out of the site's own genuinely-rendered navigation data (root page VisualNavigationItem tiles, or the Christmas Trees leaf's own SideNavigation sidebar - the same sidebar Home Depot renders across its Christmas/Holiday leaf pages), which per rules.md SS2/SS12 is the strongest form of category evidence (main navigation / category tree), not a guess from a URL slug or marketing copy. Claude-in-Chrome (Tier 3 / last resort) was also attempted for the blocked ?catStyle=ShowProducts grid view but the shared browser tab-group was unresponsive/flaky (a shared multi-worker Chrome session with tabs from other concurrent tasks already open; tab creation and navigation calls errored or hung) and was abandoned as not a reliable route right now, in favor of what had already been recovered via curl_cffi. EXCLUDED CANDIDATES (logged to qa_notes.md, not fabricated as rows): (1) three Halloween tiles - 'Licensed Characters', 'Halloween Pumpkins', 'Tombstones' - use a visibly different URL pattern from every other genuine leaf here (an extra Z-suffixed refinement code appended to the parent Halloween N-code, e.g. N-5yc1vZc2veZ1z23ga2, vs. every other leaf's clean single N-code) strongly suggesting these are facet/filter views of the Halloween Decorations listing rather than distinct taxonomy nodes - per rules SS17 'filter-only pages' are excluded, and this could not be live-confirmed either way before the WAF re-block, so excluded rather than guessed; (2) the site's generic 'Seasonal Decorations' branch (Wreaths & Garlands, Porch & Yard Decorations, Indoor Seasonal Decorations, 'Shop All Seasons', 'Decorations Savings') is a multi-holiday/all-season catch-all bucket, not tied to one specific festival - excluded per the rules SS3 Diwali/Festive-style ambiguity warning (a generic seasonal label whose holiday association can't be pinned down), logged for adjudication rather than force-assigned to Christmas or dropped silently; (3) 'Party Decorations' (Holiday-Decorations-Party-Decorations/N-5yc1vZch2a) is filed under the Holiday Decorations department by Home Depot's own taxonomy but its own marketing copy ('Independence Day, Halloween, Hanukkah, Christmas, Fall...') shows it spans every occasion generically rather than belonging to one holiday, so it has no single `category` value under this schema - excluded, logged; (4) checked page marketing copy for Easter/Valentine/Diwali/Thanksgiving/New Year/Eid/Rakhi/St. Patrick's - all either absent entirely or present only as incidental prose mentions ('Independence Day, Halloween, Hanukkah, Christmas...Fall...New Year's Eve') with zero corresponding nav tile or category URL - correctly excluded as marketing-copy-only, not a dedicated category (rules SS4/SS17).
